learning_outcomes.text: Possess knowledge about energy forms, measurement, and conversion.
Learn the physical operating principles of sensors and transducers.
Be able to select sensors and transducers according to the industrial system.
Be able to perform sensor and transducer connections.
Be able to design and implement data acquisition/processing circuits.
Be able to perform signal scaling and interpret the obtained results.

syllabus_topics: Energy forms, signal domains, measurement systems, units and standards, sensing and conversion principles
Types and classification of sensors and transducers, connection types and standards
Interface circuits used with sensors, bridge circuits, differential amplifier circuits, gain circuits, filter circuits

Thermal sensors and transducers (RTD, thermocouple, thermostat, bimetal, laser, optical-based temperature sensors, pyrometers, thermistors, semiconductor-based temperature sensors and infrared technologies)
Inductive and capacitive sensors and transducers, electromagnetic field sensors and transducers
Position, level, displacement, speed, acceleration sensors and transducers, living and motion sensors
Force, strain, pressure, acoustic sensors and transducers
Solid, liquid, gas flow sensors and transducers
Light, radiation sensors and transducers, radiation sensors, fiber-optic based technologies
Humidity and chemical sensors and transducers
Analog-digital and digital-analog converters and resolution designs, considerations for sensor selection
Smart sensor technologies, introduction to computer-aided data acquisition units and programs (Data Acquisition Systems)
assessment_rules: Midterm and final exam dates are not specified in the 14-week course plan. Midterm and final exam dates are held on the dates specified in the academic calendar by the decision of the University Senate.
